title: Container Bookings: Containers on Which a Destination Change Is Charged
content:
The change-of-destination fee of Container Bookings is levied per container, but not on every container the booking lists. This page defines the containers that count.

## Rule

The fee is levied only on containers the line will actually carry. Containers covered by a dangerous-goods acceptance of the booking that the line has rejected, as shown by the rejected status on the acceptance record, will not sail and are left out. The chargeable containers are thus the container quantity of the booking less the container count of that rejected acceptance, with zero as the lowest possible figure. A booking with no rejected acceptance has nothing taken off.

A product that does not permit a change of port of discharge never accepts one, so under such a product there are no chargeable containers and no fee.

A booking on which the line has rejected more than one dangerous-goods acceptance lies outside these rules, since they do not define its chargeable containers.

## Hypothetical cases

| Booking quantity | Rejected acceptance on the booking | Product permits destination change | Chargeable containers |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | none | yes | 10 |
| 10 | one, covering 3 containers | yes | 7 |
| 4 | one, covering 6 containers | yes | 0 |
| 10 | none | no | 0 |
| 10 | two rejected acceptances | yes | not defined by these rules |

The quantities are invented; the acceptance status and container counts come from the dangerous-goods acceptance records of the booking.
